title: Escape The Ghosts
summary: In an infinite 2-D grid, you begin at the point [0, 0] and your goal is to reach a target located at [xtarget, ytarget].
statement: In an infinite 2-D grid, you begin at the point [0, 0] and your goal is to reach a target located at [xtarget, ytarget]. The ghosts start at several specified points, which are provided in a 2D array named ghosts. Each element in the array ghosts[i] = [xi, yi] represents the starting position of the i^th ghost. On each turn, you and all the ghosts can independently choose to move 1 unit in any of the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, or west) or choose to stay still. You are considered to have escaped if you reach the target before any ghost reaches your current position. If you and a ghost reach any square (including the target) at the same time, you do not escape. Return true if you can always escape, regardless of how the ghosts move, otherwise return false.
constraints: All players move one Manhattan step per turn and ghosts may wait.
Return whether the player from [0,0] can reach target before every ghost.
hints: A ghost can always head directly to the target and wait there.
Compare the player’s Manhattan distance with every ghost’s distance to target.
Escape only if each ghost distance is strictly greater than the player distance.
If a ghost arrives no later it blocks the target; otherwise the player’s direct shortest route finishes first.
editorial: If a ghost arrives no later it blocks the target; otherwise the player’s direct shortest route finishes first.

tests.explanation: The player needs one move while each ghost needs at least two.
The ghost reaches the target in one move, no later than the player.
